clue.text: A pronounced sensitivity is criticised

indicators.note: pronounced says the phrase 'a' plus the word for sensitivity is spoken, giving a word that only sounds the same

parts.note: tact is sensitivity in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Someone's noticeable touchiness comes in for criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a tact' runs together into a past tense meaning criticised, so the spoken TACT is written TTACKED after the A; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be criticised harshly is to be verbally assailed, a common figurative synonym.

clue.text: Deceptive, our silly manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters of the preceding words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's silly tactics are misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges OUR SILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deceptive gives a false impression, as an illusion does; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Far right give vent to feelings

parts.note: to emote is to display feelings theatrically

explanation.surface: A politician on the far right lets rip with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far right' looks like a political phrase, but 'Far' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote and far both describe something a long distance away; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Suitable site developed with these?

parts.note: proper means suitable or appropriate

indicators.note: developed means the letters of site are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A property developer's question: what does one build on a good plot?
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges SITE into TIES; the whole clue also describes buildings put up on a suitable site.
explanation.definitionFit: Developers build houses and other real estate on a plot, so the buildings are what a site is developed with.

clue.text: After opening, accidentally lose some medicine

indicators.note: after the opening means the word is used once its first letter has gone

parts.note: to spill a liquid is to lose some of it accidentally

explanation.surface: Once the bottle is open, some medicine gets spilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After opening' strips the S from SPILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a single dose of medicine, so a little piece of medicine fits.

clue.text: Unearths an extraordinary stage work

indicators.note: extraordinary, read as out of the ordinary, tells us the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An archaeologist digs up a remarkable piece of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges UNEARTHS AN. Tannhauser is Wagner's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's Tannhauser is an opera, a work written for performance on stage.

clue.text: One given new coat: no extremes of dress, may I ask?

indicators.note: no extremes means the word is used without its first and last letters

parts.note: pray is an old polite way of asking, as in pray tell

explanation.surface: Someone queries a dress being shortened at both ends before a new coat goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no extremes of' trims DRESS to RES. The definition is a noun: a car that has had a respray has been given a new coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A respray is a fresh coat of paint applied to a vehicle, so the noun is a coating renewed.

clue.text: Conspirator puts sons through college

indicators.note: putting one thing through another places it inside
putting one thing through another places it inside

parts.note: Caius is a Cambridge college
S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons give two of them

explanation.surface: A plotter sends his boys to university.
explanation.walkthrough: Gonville and Caius is a Cambridge college, usually just called Caius and pronounced 'keys'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassius was one of the plotters who killed Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Diner finally cuts into meat that is way the most uneven in quality

indicators.note: cuts into means the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: steak is a cut of meat

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A diner carves into the most unevenly cooked steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from Diner, and 'cuts into' puts it inside STEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Something streaky is patchy or variable, so the superlative means most variable in quality.

clue.text: Atmosphere in restaurant

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the next word

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the ambience in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside restAURAnt.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive feeling surrounding a place or person, its atmosphere.

clue.text: One's quiet, on edge at this point in a half of football?

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after what follows it

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth
one is I, and the 's adds S
p is piano, quiet in music
here means at this point

explanation.surface: A commentator notes the side keeping quiet and nervous during one half of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: A football is a sphere, so half of it is a half-sphere; the question mark flags the pun on 'half'.
explanation.definitionFit: Half of any sphere, a football included, is a hemisphere: a pun on the match's halves.

clue.text: Surrounded by some poor visibility, died in it

indicators.note: in it means the letter goes inside the phrase just given

parts.note: a mist is some poor visibility

explanation.surface: Someone died in the middle of a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts D inside A MIST, with 'it' pointing back to the mist.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the middle of things is to be surrounded by them; a preposition for a preposition.

clue.text: Wretched person beset by low, droning irritant

indicators.note: beset by means the person is surrounded by the following word

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
a squit is British slang for a contemptible small person

explanation.surface: A miserable individual is surrounded by a low-level whining nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's moo, not the adjective. SQUIT is British slang for an insignificant person.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect is known for its whining buzz and itchy bites, a droning pest.

clue.text: Look at extremely gloomy books or play

parts.note: to peer at is to look closely

indicators.note: extremely picks the outermost letters of the word after it

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: An invitation to browse gloomy books or a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives GY from gloomy. Peer Gynt is Ibsen's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's Peer Gynt is a verse drama, so it is an instance of a play.

clue.text: Point about part of film that shows limit to growth

indicators.note: about places the first word round the second

parts.note: a tine is a point or prong of a fork or antler
a reel is a spool holding part of a film

explanation.surface: A critic points to a part of a film showing how far things can grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' tempts as a definition, but it is the prong; 'that shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The altitude on a mountain above which trees cannot grow is a boundary to growth.

clue.text: This last book now is a film

definitions.text: This last book now is a film

parts.words: This last book now is a film
parts.note: the final book of the Bible, Revelation, has another name that with 'now' added is a Coppola war film

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the final book has been adapted for the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The last book of the Bible is also called by this name, and Coppola's Vietnam film adds 'Now'.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation, the Bible's final book, is also known by this Greek-derived name meaning unveiling.

clue.text: Don't tell anyone I don't want dawn to break

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning keep a secret

definitions.text: I don't want dawn to break
definitions.meaning: read literally, a wish for the night to stay unlit

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition takes the idiom literally: keeping things unlit so dawn never comes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keep something secret, and read literally means keep the light out.

clue.text: Has nothing to do with hills one's in

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the hills

parts.note: the Downs are chalk hills of southern England
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone avoids the hills where they live.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are ranges of low chalk hills in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse any connection with them, so to have nothing to do with them.

clue.text: One calving, perhaps — smooth progress heard

indicators.note: heard says the word for smooth progress is taken as spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: flow is smooth, steady progress

explanation.surface: A farmer hears a cow calving went smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: Calving here is ice breaking off, not a cow giving birth; ice sheets calve icebergs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of floating ice may shed chunks, which is called calving; the 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Disputed book's so very much loved?

definitions.meaning: the Book of Tobit is apocryphal, of disputed canonical status; the 's adds the S

explanation.walkthrough: Tobit is in the Apocrypha, accepted by some churches but not others, hence 'disputed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loving someone to bits means loving them hugely, and Tobit's is an apocryphal biblical book's.

clue.text: Point on flower coming up in certainly unattractive prospects

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above what follows

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: in puts the reversed flower inside the word for certainly

parts.note: yes means certainly

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rose is a flower

explanation.surface: Someone affirms a bloom sprouting, yet the views are ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the bloom here, not a river; 'coming up' gives ESOR in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly sights spoil a view, so the plural means unsightly vistas.

clue.text: One blooming fellow's comfort, taking in culture!

indicators.note: taking in means the following word goes inside

parts.note: he is a fellow, and the 's adds S
art is culture
ease is comfort

explanation.surface: A man finds solace in the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartsease is the wild pansy; 'One blooming' looks like an expletive but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartsease, the wild pansy, is a flowering plant, so it is something in bloom.

clue.text: Ready for toast, honest

definitions.meaning: on one's feet, as diners rise to drink a toast

explanation.definitionFit: Standing up to toast, and morally upright: both senses of the adjective.

clue.text: Most here refurbished an old institution

indicators.note: refurbished means the letters are done up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Refurbishing turns a building here into a time-honoured establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refurbished' rearranges MOST HERE. 'old' means for old people, not ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential care home is a facility for elderly people, an institution for the old.

clue.text: Lack of logic: answer is found in decay of neurons

indicators.note: is found in places the letter inside what follows
decay breaks down the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Irrationality explained as neurons decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decay of' turns NEURONS into UNRESON, and A goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is irrationality, the absence of sound reasoning.

clue.text: Daughter, look after our mother — pressure is to grow

indicators.note: look comes after our mother in the answer

parts.note: Eve is the mother of all humans in Genesis
lo means look, as in lo and behold
p is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A daughter cares for her mother under strain, needing to mature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to grow or mature over time.

clue.text: Negligent teacher of religion?

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, a school subject
Miss is how British pupils address a female teacher

explanation.surface: A careless religious instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: British pupils call a female teacher 'Miss'; RE is the school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remiss means being careless about one's duties.

clue.text: Result when one's smashed in face

definitions.text: Result when one's smashed in face

indicators.note: smashed in means the letter is forced inside

parts.note: pan is slang for face
one is I; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Being punched in the face hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan is slang for face; the whole clue describes the hurt too.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck in the face causes hurt, so the suffering follows the blow.
